sections.title: The group kn
paragraphs: The letters kn make one single sound. You hear this sound at the start of (knee) /ni/, the part of the leg. It has only one sound in English.

sections.title: Making the sound
paragraphs: Press the tip of your tongue against the ridge behind your top teeth. Lower the soft roof of your mouth so air flows through your nose. Turn your voice on. Touch your throat to feel it shake. The sound is a voiced nasal, which is a sound where air goes out through the nose.

sections.title: Where kn appears
paragraphs: The group kn appears at the beginning of words. In this group, the first letter is a silent letter, which means a letter that you write but do not say. You only say the second consonant, like in (knot) /nɒt/.

sections.title: Avoiding extra sounds
paragraphs: Never say an extra plosive before the nasal sound. A plosive is a consonant where the air stops and bursts out. Keep your mouth still and start straight with the nasal sound. Do not say a sound like the k in cat.
